newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen tendering for corn, soybeans, wheat.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen tendering for corn, soybeans, wheat.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected to hold three tenders next week for a total of 72,000 tonnes of corn, 12,000 tonnes of soybeans and between 64,000 tonnes and 96,000 tonnes of wheat, local traders said on Friday.
Traders expect state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp to tender for a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 U.S. soybeans.
Taiwan Sugar's shipment is slated for delivery from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico from October 25 to November 10, they said.
Taiwan's FGEP corn buying group is expected to tender for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn.
The FGEP shipment would be scheduled for delivery from December 10-25 from the U.S. Gulf or between December 26 to January 9 from the Pacific Northwest.
Local buyers said pressure from the U.S. corn harvest and the favourable weather in the Midwest could send Chicago corn prices down to test price support at US$2.70 a bushel.
"The corn is still bearish for the harvest season with no serious frost expected," an executive at Taiwan's Formosa Oilseeds said.
Taiwan's soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was T$9.8 to T$10.0 a kg, up from T$9.6 to T$9.8 a week earlier.
Corn powder was priced at T$7.17 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from T$7.25 to T$7.30 a kg a week earlier.

Local Pacific Northwest to Taiwan freight costs were quoted at about US$11.00 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at between US$18.50 to US$19.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized November and December shipments.
Taiwan's Flour Mills Association may place tenders next week for two or three 34,000-tonne shipments of U.S. wheat, an association official said.
"We are arranging fourth quarter supplies and could place a tender soon," he told Reuters, adding that between two or three shipments were being considered.
Wheat flour was quoted between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
